Chapter 10. Reflections on Survival, Identity, and What Really Matters.
Looking back, you realize the journey—from being that restless kid to becoming a world champion, and then from cancer patient to survivor—was never just a straight line. There were detours, setbacks that felt impossible, and a few unexpected blessings along the way.
The bike? At first, it was everything. But over time, it turned into so much more. It became a way to explore not just how far your body could go, but how deep your spirit could reach. It brought connections—real ones—with people you might never have met otherwise. And honestly, it helped reveal what truly matters.
Survival changes everything. It strips away any illusion you had about being in control, and suddenly, you see just how fragile—and beautiful—life really is. You're forced to ask yourself, "Who am I, when everything else is taken away?" For some folks, that answer comes through achievement—pushing boundaries, chasing big dreams. For others, it lives in the quiet moments: time with people you love, helping someone out, or simply feeling grateful to wake up and breathe another day.
The truth is, this journey was never just about the bike. It was about resilience. It was about finding the courage to keep moving forward, even when fear and uncertainty tried to slow you down. It was about the people who stood by you during the darkest times, the lessons you learned while fighting through illness and recovery, and the realization that real strength isn't about never falling—it’s about getting back up, every single time you do.
